sources.title: Brewing Sour and Wild Ales (incl. 'The Falcon Method For Fermenting Lambics', credited to MB Raines)
sources.supports: Brettanomyces species characters — B. claussenii/anomalus (English stock beer origin, softer, pineapple and mango), B. bruxellensis (Brussels, medium earthy funk), B. lambicus (every lambic, huge horsey character with fruitiness, smoky and sour). Lactobacillus delbrueckii: lactic acid for crisp dry acidity, primary character of Berliner Weisse, ferment very warm e.g. 98 °F. Pediococcus: large lactic production from glucose, no CO2, massive diacetyl charge in early ferment. Acetobacter as 'vinegar mother' converting ethanol to acetic acid. Enterobacter contributing bilious characters. Timeline: at least a month before cultures show character, optimally six months to a year. Named blends WLP655, Wyeast 3278, Wyeast 3763 Roeselare.
sources.doesNotSupport: Temperature ranges, attenuation, flocculation or alcohol tolerance for any of these organisms except the single 98 °F figure for L. delbrueckii.

The ISBN is the identifier a future page-level check would use. The numeric yeast specs this project ships are transcribed from the yeast producers' own spec sheets (White Labs, Wyeast, Lallemand, Omega, Fermentis), which are the primary measurements this book itself synthesises.

sources.title: Notes from the Field: Botulism from Drinking Prison-Made Illicit Alcohol in Utah, 2011
sources.publisher: Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report 62(07):138, US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.supports: An outbreak of foodborne botulism among prisoners who drank pruno; eight hospitalised; type A botulinum toxin identified; a weeks-old baked potato implicated as the spore source. Establishes pruno as a documented public-health hazard rather than folklore.
sources.doesNotSupport: Any production method, ingredient ratio or yield. This project cites it to describe and warn, not to instruct.

sources.title: The Microbial Diversity of Traditional Spontaneously Fermented Lambic Beer
sources.supports: The microbiology of spontaneous lambic fermentation, from over 2000 isolates sampled over two years at a traditional Belgian lambic brewery. No yeast is pitched: cooled overnight in an open coolship, the wort is inoculated by the ambient microbiota of the Senne valley, then matures 1-3 years before bottling. A characteristic succession follows: Enterobacteriaceae dominate the first month (~3-40 days), replaced at ~2 months by Pediococcus damnosus with Saccharomyces cerevisiae and S. pastorianus, then from ~6 months onward by the acid- and ethanol-tolerant Dekkera bruxellensis alongside P. damnosus. DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0095384. Underpins the beer-spontaneous fermentation archetype.
sources.doesNotSupport: Pitch rates (there is no pitch), or the microbiota of any other region's spontaneous ferment; it documents traditional Belgian lambic specifically.
sources.note: Peer-reviewed open-access literature; cited for the microbial succession of spontaneous lambic fermentation (Spitaels et al. 2014).

sources.title: Active Dry Wine Yeast (ADWY) rehydration
sources.supports: The professional wine-yeast inoculation standard: an inoculum of 0.25 g/L (25 g/hL) of active dry wine yeast to achieve a minimum 5×10^6 viable cells/mL; rehydrate by sprinkling over 5-10 times its weight of 38-40 C water and standing 10-15 minutes; up to about twice the dose for highly clarified, high-Brix or high-SO2 musts. Underpins the wine-cultured fermentation archetype.
sources.doesNotSupport: Beer/cider/mead pitch rates, or any wild-ferment figure. It is the wine active-dry-yeast standard specifically.
sources.note: National wine research body; its winemaking-resources pages are authoritative professional guidance. Source of the 25 g/hL active-dry-wine-yeast inoculation standard.

sources.title: 125th Anniversary Review: Bacteria in brewing — the good, the bad and the ugly
sources.publisher: Journal of the Institute of Brewing 118:335-345
sources.supports: Lactobacillus brevis and Pediococcus damnosus as the lactic acid bacteria most commonly implicated in beer spoilage; L. brevis among the most hop-tolerant; hop iso-alpha-acids as ionophores impairing proton motive force; beer typically carrying 17-55 ppm iso-alpha-acids as an intrinsic antimicrobial hurdle.

sources.title: WildBrew Philly Sour — Technical Data Sheet
sources.supports: Lachancea thermotolerans, pure active dried strain; attenuation 74-82%; 20-30 °C (68-86 °F), optimal 25-30 °C (77-86 °F); flocculation high; alcohol tolerance 9% ABV; pitching 50-150 g/hL; viability >=1x10^9 CFU/g; POF negative; diastaticus negative; killer negative; aroma sour, red apple, stone fruit, peach; fermentation completable in 10 days at 20 °C.
sources.doesNotSupport: Species-wide behaviour of L. thermotolerans outside this product; titratable acidity figures are quoted in Lallemand standard-conditions wort only.

sources.title: The yeast Kluyveromyces marxianus and its biotechnological potential
sources.supports: Lactose assimilation and fermentation; thermotolerance with maximum growth temperature variously reported as 47 °C (Anderson et al. 1986), 49 °C (Hughes et al. 1984) and 52 °C (Banat et al. 1992); ethanol production above 40 °C; LOWER ethanol tolerance than S. cerevisiae, correlated with plasma-membrane ATPase activity (Rosa & Sá-Correia 1992); Crabtree-negative and facultatively fermentative; cannot grow under strictly anaerobic conditions, with ethanol formation almost exclusively linked to oxygen availability.
sources.doesNotSupport: Any single numeric alcohol tolerance for the species. The 10% v/v figure circulating for K. marxianus comes from strains after ~100 days of directed adaptive evolution and is not a native specification.

background.title: Dampfbier, Bayerisch
background.publisher: GradPlato — Fachverlag Hans Carl GmbH, Nürnberg
background.supports: Historical Dampfbier as a top-fermented, medium-dark barley-malt beer of the Bayerischer Wald near the Bohemian border, popular toward the end of the 19th century and brewed predominantly in summer. Modern versions deep gold to light amber, medium body, hopped only very lightly to about 15 BE, low carbonation ('wenig Rezenz'), fermented fast and warm with ordinary Weissbier yeast at about 21 °C, giving a slightly phenolic and banana-like finish — 'quasi ein Weißbier ohne Weizen'. Name derived from the large foam bubbles thrown by a vigorous open-vessel primary fermentation, which looked as though the wort were giving off steam as each burst. May be filtered or unfiltered. One published recipe's targets: Stammwürze 12 °P, Restextrakt 2.5 °P, 14 BE, 10 EBC, 5.1 % alcohol by volume; Hallertauer Mittelfrüh at 4.25 % alpha for both bittering and aroma; infusion mash 67 °C/30 min, 72 °C/20 min, 76 °C for lautering; 60 min boil; ferment ~4 days at ~21 °C; krausen with reserved wort; spund at ~0.5 bar for a week, a further week under pressure, adjust to ~3.5 g/L CO2. Records that the Dampfbierbrauerei Zwiesel brews a Dampfbier to a historical recipe.
background.doesNotSupport: Any style RANGE. Every figure above is a single formulation's target, not a measured minimum and maximum across the style, and no judging body catalogues Dampfbier for one to be taken from. Also does not support a malt bill: the page's percentage column is internally inconsistent — Pilsner 35 % / Münchner 1 25 % sums to 60 %, not the stated 100 %, while its kilogram column (2.71 + 1.16 = 3.87 kg) is self-consistent and implies roughly 70 % / 30 %. The percentages are therefore not transcribed into this project. The page is bylined 'Jule' and does NOT credit Horst Dornbusch; the shared publisher is circumstantial and is not treated as authorship.

background.title: Stile mit Geschichte – Folge 16: Dampfbier – Wenn's in der Brauerei zischt und brodelt
background.supports: Qualitative corroboration only, and only where it agrees with a better source: origin in Niederbayern and the Bayerischer Wald, where 19th-century brewers had little means of cooling and so treated top-fermented beer like lager; top-fermenting yeast worked unusually warm, often in open vessels, throwing a wild foaming fermentation that appeared to steam; the style nearly died out, kept alive by a few breweries (it names Hutthurmer and Lang-Bräu) and revived occasionally as a historical style; malt-forward, fruity-spicy, with some yeast character, neither heavy nor sweet; pale barley malt with small roast-malt additions, moderate regional hops such as Hallertauer, house top-fermenting strains, soft to medium-hard water. Also notes that Anchor Steam's warm-fermentation origin is a parallel response to the same lack of refrigeration and not a direct relation.
background.doesNotSupport: Every number it prints. Unbylined and uncited, so tertiary, which in this project can never carry a numeric specification. Its 20-30 IBU and 4.8-5.2 % ABV figures are recorded in the style entry as a DISAGREEMENT with the Hans Carl recipe's 14 BE rather than averaged or merged into it.

background.title: Horst Dornbusch — biography and bibliography
background.publisher: horstdornbusch.com (author's own site); bibliography cross-checked against German Wikipedia
background.supports: Horst Dornbusch, born 1947 in Düsseldorf, German-American brewing consultant, brewer and technical author; founder of Cerevisia Communications LLC; won a Great American Beer Festival bronze medal for an Altbier; Associate Editor and a major contributor to The Oxford Companion to Beer (Oxford University Press). His German beer-style works, whose ISBNs are the durable identifiers: 'Das große BRAUWELT Lexikon der Biersorten' (Fachverlag Hans Carl, Nürnberg, 2017, ISBN 978-3-418-00131-9) and 'Die Biersorten der BRAUWELT. Ihre Geschichten & Rezepturen' (Fachverlag Hans Carl, Nürnberg, ISBN 978-3-418-00126-5); in English, 'Prost! The Story of German Beer' (Brewers Publications, 1997, ISBN 978-0-937381-55-7), 'Altbier' (1998, ISBN 978-0-937381-62-5), 'Bavarian Helles' (2000, ISBN 978-0-937381-73-1), 'The Ultimate Almanac of World Beer Recipes' (2010, ISBN 978-0984444908), 'Beer Styles from Around the World' (2015, ISBN 978-0984444922).
background.doesNotSupport: Any beer style specification whatsoever. Neither the site nor the Wikipedia article reproduces the germanbeerinstitute.com style pages, and the books' contents have not been consulted — this entry exists so the bibliography is on record as the place a future verification would have to go, not as a citation for any figure. Note also that German Wikipedia misprints the year of the 'Biersorten der BRAUWELT' edition as 1916.

background.supports: That Horst Dornbusch authored 'Das große BRAUWELT Lexikon der Biersorten' (2017), an A-to-Z inventory of world beer styles from antiquity to the present covering classic styles, craft-era beers and the most significant historical styles, deliberately written with minimal brew-science vocabulary, and that the author explicitly claims no completeness.
